goal.objective: Build a new automated factory that continuously produces at least one automation-science-pack per game minute from natural resources.

definition.summary: Build a new automated factory that continuously produces at least one automation-science-pack per game minute from natural resources.

review_notes.goal_1ds0xn5_1_p3_v1_s3_08aozp4: Continue the unchanged active step. The fresh drill inspection confirms it is working, holds 4 coal, covers iron ore, and drops directly into furnace 30. Do not refuel or rebuild the drill unnecessarily. The furnace’s no_ingredients status does not establish fuel depletion: this slower direct-fed cell can leave the furnace waiting between ore deliveries. Inspect the furnace’s current fuel and output, replenish its fuel from the 10 held coal only if needed, and verify both machines working during an ore-processing cycle. Preserve the existing direct-feed arrangement; do not replace the committed checkpoint or claim completion from fuel transfers alone.

nodes.why_it_matters: Establish a new direct-fed iron cell, obtain at least 50 iron plates in inventory, and verify steam-power through its native production trigger of 50 iron plates. The live research graph reports this trigger independently ready. Automatic fuel delivery is a separate milestone.

Establish a new natural-resource copper mining and smelting cell and verify electronics through its native production trigger of 10 copper plates. Determine its construction materials from fresh recipes before committing its slice.

nodes.why_it_matters: Verify both electronics and steam-power are researched before crafting the currently locked lab. Produce one lab to satisfy the exact automation-science-pack technology trigger and verify that technology is researched.

After steam-power is researched, build a new water-to-steam electrical supply and verify it powers a real load. Its slice must separate pump installation, boiler connection, engine connection, and electrical operation at fresh geometry boundaries.

After automation-science-pack research unlocks the recipe, produce the ten required initial packs and supply a powered lab. Verify automation research is completed before crafting or building assembling-machine-1.

Establish natural-resource fuel extraction and automatic delivery to the selected burner machines and steam generation. Verify actual delivery routes so recurring manual fueling is unnecessary. Check any machinery unlocks before construction.

After automation research, route automatically mined and smelted iron into powered gear assembly. Verify actual ingredient delivery and enough output for the science target using live recipe rates and transport measurements.

Connect automatic copper and gear supply to powered science assembly and automatic output removal. Validate transport capacity and sustain at least one automation-science-pack per minute over ten minutes without hand-fed ingredients. Do not impose an artificial science stock cap.

steps.description: Acquire a bootstrap reserve of at least 20 coal for the held iron miner and furnace.

execution_guidance.approach: Gather coal until at least 20 are held; retain this initial reserve for the iron cell.
execution_guidance.rationale: Both buildings are already held, avoiding construction-material costs. This is finite startup fuel, not the final automated fuel supply.
constraints: Use the actual inventory deficit.
Do not remove player-built structures.
Acquire additional fuel later only if needed.

steps.description: Install one held burner-mining-drill covering natural iron ore; observe its new exact identity and actual output position.

execution_guidance.approach: Use the held drill on natural iron with native resource-covering placement validation; observe its actual output before placing the furnace.
execution_guidance.rationale: Choose direct feed: the held drill yields 15 ore/min versus 30 by hand, but works during other tasks and avoids repeated hand supply. No extra drill investment is justified for this first cell.
constraints: Use one held burner-mining-drill.
Validate live iron coverage.
Stop at the new identity and output boundary.

steps.description: Install the held stone-furnace to receive the drill’s output, fuel both machines, and verify both are working.

execution_guidance.approach: Place the held furnace over the observed drill output; fuel both and verify direct output connectivity and working status.
execution_guidance.rationale: Reusing the held furnace avoids crafting cost. Automatic ore feed supports the larger factory goal; hand-fed smelting would require repeated intervention despite its lower setup effort.
constraints: Confirm live iron-smelting compatibility.
Use fresh exact identities for both machines.
Verify the drill output targets this furnace.

steps.description: Collect at least 50 iron plates into inventory and verify steam-power is researched through its native 50-iron-plate production trigger.

execution_guidance.approach: Let the direct-fed cell produce, collect plates, replenish startup fuel if necessary, and verify the exact steam-power trigger result.
execution_guidance.rationale: Fifty new plates require at least 200 seconds of this drill’s mining time. Keep the single held cell working rather than pay for uncosted expansion; its output also supports later construction.
constraints: Do not hand-craft iron plates.
Verify inventory and researched state separately.
Keep the new iron cell available for later routing.

steps.description: Acquire at least 10 stone and 20 coal for the copper cell’s construction and startup fuel.

execution_guidance.approach: Acquire the deficits for 10 stone and 20 coal using natural sources; use finite-product harvesting for suitable rocks or ordinary gathering for resource patches.
execution_guidance.rationale: Ten stone covers two furnace crafts: one furnace is consumed by the drill. Twenty coal provides startup fuel, not permanent automatic fuel delivery.
constraints: Compute deficits from fresh inventory.
Use natural sources rather than dismantling buildings.
Do not assume a particular rock yield.

steps.description: Craft one burner-mining-drill and one additional stone-furnace, retaining at least 20 coal.

execution_guidance.approach: Resolve bootstrap dependencies and craft three gears, two furnaces and one drill, leaving one furnace and the coal reserve held.
execution_guidance.rationale: The combined construction bill is 9 iron plates and 10 stone; the fresh inventory contains 50 iron plates. No extra cells are needed for this milestone.
constraints: Resolve the exact first missing dependency before downstream crafting.
Verify both finished kit items.
Retain at least 20 coal.

steps.description: Install the new drill covering natural copper ore; inspect its exact identity, resource coverage and actual output position.

execution_guidance.approach: Place the new drill on natural copper using resource-covering placement validation, then inspect its new identity and output geometry.
execution_guidance.rationale: Direct feed yields 15 ore/min versus 30/min by hand. Ten ore alone favors manual work, but the 9-iron, 10-stone setup creates continuing supply and avoids repeated mining and hand delivery.
constraints: Preserve the existing iron cell and its direct-feed route.
Confirm actual copper resource coverage.
Stop before furnace placement needs the new output observation.

steps.description: Install the new furnace to receive the copper drill’s observed output; inspect the resulting direct-feed connection.

execution_guidance.approach: Use the observed copper drill output to select a furnace placement covering that point; inspect the new furnace and drill connection afterward.
execution_guidance.rationale: A stone furnace can smelt 18.75 copper plates/min, exceeding this drill’s 15 ore/min. One pair suffices; a larger smelting row adds unnecessary startup cost.
constraints: Preserve the iron cell and the new copper drill.
Verify the drill actually targets the new furnace.
Placement counts prove presence, not operation.

steps.description: Fuel the copper cell, collect at least 10 copper plates, and verify electronics is researched through its native production trigger.

execution_guidance.approach: Fuel both copper machines, verify live operation and direct ore delivery, collect ten plates, and verify the electronics trigger result.
execution_guidance.rationale: Ten plates require at least 40 seconds of drill mining and 32 seconds of furnace work, overlapping through direct feed. Coal burn is 2.25/min for the drill and at most 1.35/min for the furnace.
constraints: Use fresh exact copper-machine identities for transfers.
Do not substitute hand-fed ore for direct mining.
Verify electronics completion, not a research request.

steps.description: Collect copper plates from the existing direct-fed copper cell until inventory holds at least 15, preserving the drill and furnace connection.

execution_guidance.approach: Collect the copper-plate deficit from the existing furnace, retaining the drill-to-furnace route; replenish fuel only if necessary.
execution_guidance.rationale: Reuse the working cell with no setup cost. At 15 ore/min the five-plate deficit takes about 20 seconds of mining; another cell or manual ore delivery is unnecessary for this small bootstrap.
constraints: Refresh exact furnace output and fuel before transfer.
Preserve drill 31 feeding furnace 32.
Do not build another cell or hand-feed copper ore.

steps.description: Craft one lab and verify automation-science-pack technology is researched through its native lab-production trigger.

execution_guidance.approach: Resolve missing intermediates, craft one lab, and verify the automation-science-pack technology's lab-production trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: One lab requires a combined 36 iron plates and 15 copper plates: 12 gears, 30 cable, 10 circuits and four belts. The held 41 iron plates cover the bill; retain the lab for powered research later.
constraints: Resolve live bootstrap dependencies before downstream crafts.
Verify one lab held and the technology researched.
Do not craft locked science packs or assemblers in this slice.

steps.description: Collect iron plates from the existing direct-fed iron cell until inventory holds at least 42, preserving the existing smelting cells.

execution_guidance.approach: Return to the iron cell at (-66, 7), refresh its identities, fuel and output, and collect the plate deficit without changing the direct-feed route.
execution_guidance.rationale: The held five plates leave a 37-plate deficit. Reusing the existing cell avoids another miner/furnace setup and repeated manual ore delivery. Additional smelting capacity is optional, not needed for this kit.
constraints: Refresh the iron drill identity and verify its actual furnace drop target.
Preserve the existing machines and native item routes.
Replenish fuel only as needed; verify 42 plates held before kit crafting.

steps.description: Prepare and verify one offshore pump, one boiler, one steam engine, two small electric poles, ten coal and the existing lab, preserving the existing smelting cells.

execution_guidance.approach: Acquire missing materials, resolve crafting intermediates and prepare the core steam kit, retaining the lab and restoring held coal to ten.
execution_guidance.rationale: The combined construction bill is 42 iron plates, five stone, one copper plate and one wood. One pole craft yields two poles. Defer extra connecting pipes until the shoreline and fluid-port geometry are known.
constraints: Collect copper from the existing cell; refresh its output and fuel first.
Craft a new furnace for the boiler; do not consume a placed smelting furnace.
Verify kit inventory only; placement, connections and powered-load proof remain later work.
